root.note: Further back the trail is unclear. Several sources take Arabic ruzz from Greek óruza; beyond that scholars debate an Iranian language, Sanskrit or Tamil.

history: Portugal is one of Europe's great rice-eating countries: arroz de pato, arroz de marisco, arroz doce for dessert. The word came with the Arabic speakers of al-Andalus. Arabic ruzz with its article gave ar-ruzz, ‘the rice’, and Portuguese took the whole thing, article included: the a- and the double r of arroz are Arabic ar-. Many Portuguese words begin this way, like azeite and aldeia. Rice itself had a long road behind it. Greek had óruza, and scholars link the word with languages further East, but no route is secure. Italian took riso from Latin and Greek, and from Italy came French riz and English rice. They share an ancestor with arroz, but not its Arabic ‘the’.
historyEinfach: Arroz means ‘rice’. Portuguese took the word from Arabic. In Arabic, ar-ruzz means ‘the rice’. So the a- at the start of arroz is the Arabic word for ‘the’. Before that, the word came from the East, but experts don't agree on the road. English rice and French riz are related to it.

elsewhere.text: Say ar-ruzz aloud and you are very close to arroz.
English came by the Greek and Italian road, so it has no article inside it.
